Our Vision
To deliver authentic experience that people trust.
BEST HOMESTAY IN INDIA
Land of the indigenous Baiga & Gond
An exclusive and raw Farmhouse in Central India.
A beautiful, compact and comfortable base from which to explore rural life in the heart of
India. Nestled at the foot of the Maikal Hills, Sunny and Deeptie Upadhyay's Bhoramdeo
Jungle Retreat is a 2 hour drive from the modern city of Raipur, a journey that takes one
gently rolling back in time. It is a matchless and offbeat destination which offers and
promotes Tribal and rural tourism in central india.

Your Host
Sunny Upadhyay
Satendra Upadhyay more affectionately known as 'SUNNY' was born and raised in
Kawardha, and is devoted to the unique, engaging Tribes of his homeland. In his company
you will meet local villagers and forest dwelling tribes without the least formality or
awkwardness – whether at one of the colourful weekly markets, or in their enchanting
villages and homes.
On occasions these villager hosts will be so delighted by your and Sunny's visit that an
impromptu celebration may be thrown in your honor. Sunny works hard for the benefit of the
Baiga and Gonds, and his guided tours are always conducted with their welfare first and
foremost in mind.

How to Reach?
By Air
Nearest airport is at State Capital Raipur. Airport is approx. 130 Km. from Bhoramdeo Jungle Retreat. It takes approx 2 hours.
By Train
Nearest Railway Station is at State Capital Raipur. It about 130 Km. from Bhoramdeo Jungle Retreat.
By Road
It is well Connected to Raipur, Bilapsur, Rajnandgaon, Durg, Bhilai city via road and takes 2.5-3 hours.
Essentials Before your Trip
Bag Packing Tips
One backpack, sturdy duffel bag, or easily managed suitcase.
Daypack (in which you may keep water bottle/snacks/cap etc)
A pair of shoes or boots comfortable for walking
Sandals or flip flop you don't mind getting wet
Money belt or pouch
Personal medications
Waterproof case
Two pair of shorts and/or swimming trunks
December and January Nights can be considerably colder than imagined. Fires are lit, but do bring layers of warm clothing too.
